{{Short description|Problem in mathematics}}
In [[mathematics]], and particularly [[homology theory]], '''Steenrod's Problem''' (named after mathematician [[Norman Steenrod]]) is a problem concerning the realisation of [[homology class]]es by singular manifolds.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Eilenberg|first=Samuel|authorlink=Samuel Eilenberg|year=1949|title=On the problems of topology|journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]]|volume=50|issue=2 | pages=247–260|doi=10.2307/1969448|jstor=1969448 }}</ref>

==Formulation==
Let <math>M</math> be a [[closed manifold|closed]], [[oriented manifold|oriented]] manifold of dimension <math>n</math>, and let <math>[M] \in H_n(M)</math> be its orientation class. Here <math>H_n(M)</math> denotes the integral, <math>n</math>-dimensional [[homology group]] of <math>M</math>. Any [[continuous map]] <math>f\colon M\to X</math> defines an induced [[homomorphism]] <math>f_*\colon H_n(M)\to  H_n(X)</math>.<ref name="TOP">{{Citation|first=Allen|last=Hatcher| authorlink=Allen Hatcher|title=Algebraic Topology|publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]]|year=2001|isbn=0-521-79540-0}}</ref> A homology class of <math>H_n(X)</math> is called realisable if it is of the form <math>f_*[M]</math> for some manifold <math>M</math> and map <math>f:M \to X</math>. The Steenrod problem is concerned with describing the realisable homology classes of <math>H_n(X)</math>.<ref name="YUB">{{Cite web|url=https://encyclopediaofmath.org/wiki/Steenrod_problem|author=Encyclopedia of Mathematics|title=Steenrod Problem|accessdate=October 29, 2020}}</ref>

==Results==
All elements of <math>H_k(X)</math> are realisable by smooth manifolds provided <math>k\le  6</math>. Moreover, any cycle can be realized by the mapping of a [[pseudo-manifold]].<ref name="YUB"/>

The assumption that ''M'' be orientable can be relaxed. In the case of non-orientable manifolds, every homology class of <math>H_n(X,\Z_2)</math>, where <math>\Z_2</math> denotes the [[integer]]s [[Modular arithmetic|modulo]] 2, can be realized by a non-oriented manifold, <math>f\colon M^n\to X</math>.<ref name="YUB"/>

==Conclusions==
For smooth manifolds ''M'' the problem reduces to finding the form of the homomorphism <math>\Omega_n(X) \to H_n(X)</math>, where <math>\Omega_n(X)</math> is the oriented [[bordism]] group of ''X''.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Rudyak|first=Yuli B.|year=1987|title=Realization of homology classes of PL-manifolds with singularities|journal=[[Mathematical Notes]]|volume=41|issue=5|pages=417–421|doi=10.1007/bf01159869|s2cid=122228542 }}</ref> The connection between the bordism groups  <math>\Omega_*</math> and the [[Thom space]]s MSO(''k'') clarified the Steenrod problem by reducing it to the study of the homomorphisms <math>H_*(\operatorname{MSO}(k)) \to H_*(X)</math>.<ref name="YUB"/><ref name="Thom">{{Cite journal|last=Thom|first=René |authorlink=René Thom|year=1954|title=Quelques propriétés globales des variétés differentiable|journal=[[Commentarii Mathematici Helvetici]]|volume=28|pages=17–86|language=French|doi=10.1007/bf02566923|s2cid=120243638 }}</ref> In his landmark paper from 1954,<ref name="Thom"/> [[René Thom]] produced an example of a non-realisable class, <math>[M] \in H_7(X)</math>, where ''M'' is the [[Eilenberg–MacLane space]] <math>K(\Z_3\oplus \Z_3,1)</math>.
